title: MOD: stay long but small (3 sh): a sector sell-off has taken the stock to $135, ~8% above our $125 thesis break, 12 days before the Nov 3 Q2 print, the expected first standalone guide
call_reason: The published target of $161.51 is 19.5% above the $135.17 close and the research target (12m) is $200, but supervisor confidence is low and the review trims to the Sharpe-optimal size (4 to 3 sh) [1][2][3][9].
one_liner: Modine is now a pure data-center and commercial HVAC cooling company that guides data-center sales +60-80% this year and has a $4B 2027-29 capacity agreement, yet it trades at $135.17, down 26% from the $182.91 research price of Oct 5, and the latest 9.75% drop came with no company news [3][9][10][17][18][19]. We keep a small long (target $161.51, research target (12m) $200) into the Nov 3 print and Nov 18 Investor Day, with a $125 thesis break and an $89.26 stop [1][3][13][14].

thesis.point: Data-center growth is guided and partly contracted, not just hoped for.
thesis.evidence: FY26 Data Centers sales were $1,108.2M with $214.7M adj. EBITDA (19.4%); the Q1 FY27 slides guide DC sales +60-80% and DC earnings growth >85% for FY27; the 10-K expects more than $4B of DC cooling sales to one customer in CY2027-29 (~$1.3B/yr); management's medium-term DC target is 50-70%/yr.

thesis.point: Margin recovery is the near-term lever, and the Nov 3 print tests it.
thesis.evidence: Q1 FY27 DC margin fell to 14.8% on $348.6M sales because of supply shortages; hitting the >85% DC earnings guide needs ~23% DC margins in Q2-Q4. No continuing-ops guide has been issued since the Oct 1 spin; the Q1 release said the outlook would be updated after the spin closed, and the supervisor expects it with the Q2 results due after the close on Nov 3.

thesis.point: The price already discounts a lot: at $135.17 the EV is ~$7.5B, ~13.4-13.9x NTM RemainCo EBITDA vs a 20.2x filing-derived peer median.
thesis.evidence: 53,196,918 shares x $135.17 + $265.3M pro forma net debt at June 30 (8-K/A Ex.99.1 of Oct 7: $43.4M current + $276.0M long-term debt - $54.1M cash; derived) = ~$7.46B EV over ~$535-555M NTM EBITDA (supervisor estimate). The Oct 22 drop (-9.75%, from $149.78) came with no Modine filing or release; Vertiv fell ~8% and GE Vernova ~11% the same day after Meta's Q3 release, which narrowed 2026 capex upward to $135-145B but showed -$2.12B Q3 free cash flow.

variant_view: We sit between the Street and the options market. Analysts (9, Strong Buy) have a median target of $301 (low $260) on StockAnalysis, and our recency-weighted median of the individual targets is $293.67 (as of Oct 20); several were set before the Oct 1 spin and on premium multiples; our research target (12m) of $200 uses 17x EBITDA, a ~16% discount to peers justified by ~11% single-customer concentration and below-peer DC margins [1][3][18][22]. The options market's own 12-month median is $134.66, roughly today's price (it gives a 44% chance of closing above the Oct 21 mark of $149.78 and ~50% above today's $135.17); our research is more constructive because DC growth is guided and contracted [1][17][19]. The published target $161.51 weights the options market 67% and research 33% [1]. The variant is modest: we are not calling the Street's $290s, only that the stock is pricing an AI-capex down-cycle that the latest hyperscaler data (Meta raising the low end of 2026 capex) does not show [1][11].

valuation.methods: Research target (12m) $200 (supervisor, after the Oct 6 citation audit): Oct-2027 NTM RemainCo EBITDA ~$665M (median of five agent builds, corporate -$80M) x 17x = EV $11.3B, less ~$280M at-close net debt, over 54.0M diluted shares = ~$204; P/E ($665M - $85M D&A - $15M interest) x 0.76 / 54.0M = ~$7.95 x 24.5x = ~$195; blended 60/40 = ~$200. Agent research targets (12m) $175-212 (four of five at $198-212); probability-weighted scenarios bear $105-125 / base $180-212 / bull $280-315 at 25/50/25. The published 12-month target $161.51 blends the options-implied distribution (67%, median $134.66) with the research distribution (33%, median $201.33); expected value $194.93 [1][3][4][5][6][7][8].

catalysts.event: Vertiv Q3 2026 results, before the open (call 11 a.m. ET)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Closest listed DC-thermal peer; MOD traded with it on Oct 22 (VRT -7.8%, MOD -9.75%).
catalysts.watch: Thermal/liquid-cooling orders and book-to-bill, pricing, any supply commentary.

catalysts.event: Hyperscaler Q3 prints: Microsoft Oct 28 after close and Amazon Oct 29 (both company-confirmed); Alphabet expected the same week (date not found, estimated by its prior-year timing)
catalysts.why_it_moves: MOD's demand is hyperscaler capex; its anchor customer (~11% of sales) is identified as Google by a single source (Hunterbrook, whose affiliate is long MOD). Meta's print alone moved AI-infrastructure names 6-11% on Oct 22.
catalysts.watch: First 2027 capex indications, how the build-out is financed (free cash flow, debt), any digestion language.

catalysts.event: Modine Q2 FY27 results after the close; call Nov 4, 10:00 a.m. CT
catalysts.why_it_moves: First guide for the continuing business after the spin, and the test of DC margin recovery from 14.8%.
catalysts.watch: DC segment margin vs FY26's 19.4%; whether DC earnings growth >85% holds; FY27 RemainCo EBITDA (agents ~$445-462M); corporate cost vs -$23M/qtr; LTA timing; post-spin net debt.

catalysts.event: Special meeting (virtual) to rename the company Modexus Solutions; two-thirds of votes entitled to be cast required
catalysts.why_it_moves: Cosmetic; a failed vote would be an embarrassment, not a fundamental change.
catalysts.watch: Vote result; any new ticker or sector reclassification.

catalysts.event: Analyst and Investor Day (multi-year targets for the post-spin company)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Resets the medium-term growth and margin anchors that the Street's ~$290s targets rely on.
catalysts.watch: DC growth target vs the 50-70%/yr already given; DC margin target (low 20s?); capital return; customer diversification beyond the anchor.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Read-through for AI data-center build rate and for next-generation cooling design (warm-water, chiller content).
catalysts.watch: Data-center revenue guide; Rubin rack cooling specs.

catalysts.event: Hyperscaler Q4 prints with full 2027 capex guides
catalysts.why_it_moves: Sets the 2027 demand base under the $4B CY27-29 agreement.
catalysts.watch: 2027 capex growth vs the research's ~+50% base case.

catalysts.date: early Feb 2027 (prior year Feb 4 after close)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Covers Oct-Dec 2026, the last quarter before CY2027 deliveries under the capacity agreement start; checks the Q2 guide.
catalysts.watch: Readiness for CY2027 LTA shipments, DC margin, backlog.

catalysts.why_it_moves: The Jan 2026 Vera Rubin 45C warm-water ('no chillers') reveal coincided with a 17.2% intraday MOD fall on Jan 6; new rack specs can repeat that.
catalysts.watch: Chiller-free messaging, cooling content per MW for Rubin Ultra/Feynman.

risks.risk: AI-capex down-cycle or financing stress at hyperscalers (bear cases $105-125).
risks.signpost: Capex cuts or 'digestion' language on the Oct 28-29 or late-Jan prints; a close below the $125 thesis break, especially with company news.

risks.risk: Customer concentration: one technology customer was ~11% of FY26 sales (identified as Google only by Hunterbrook, whose affiliate is long MOD) and anchors the $4B agreement.
risks.signpost: Any deferral, re-scoping or dual-sourcing of the capacity agreement on the Nov 3 call or at Investor Day.

risks.risk: Execution: DC margins stuck in the mid-teens on supply and labour inefficiency; FY27 reset below the >85% DC earnings guide.
risks.signpost: Q2 DC margin well below FY26's 19.4% or a continuing-ops guide below the agents' ~$445-462M FY27 RemainCo EBITDA.

risks.risk: Technology and competition: 45C warm-water designs cut chiller content; Trane, JCI and Carrier add DC chiller capacity.
risks.signpost: Chiller-free messaging at GTC (Mar 14-18) or NVIDIA's Nov print; peer price cuts or MOD share loss.

trade.position: Hold 4 sh (~$541, 2.3% of the $23,311 book); the review trims 1 to 3 sh (~$406, 1.7%), the Sharpe-optimal size of 3.3 sh [2][34]
trade.entry: No staged entry in the current review (Sharpe-optimal sizing, target 3.28 sh); the supervisor's Oct 6 plan (half after the Q2 report, half after the Nov 18 Investor Day, 3% cap) predates that sizing rule and is not used [2][3]
trade.exit_or_add: Per the decider: three 1-sh adds, all listed at ~$118.10 (to 7 sh; its schedule targets 9 sh at $117.60), two 1-sh trims at ~$152.24, and zero shares on its schedule from the $148.69 take-profit; full exit at the $89.26 stop or on a fundamental thesis break (LTA deferral or customer loss) around $125. Add sooner only if Q2 shows DC margin back near FY26's 19.4% with the >85% DC earnings guide intact [1][2][3][20].

what_changes_our_mind: Nov 3: DC margin stays near 15% and the continuing-ops guide cuts DC earnings growth well below >85%: cut the research target and exit on the next bounce [3][16][17].
Nov 18: Investor Day DC growth target below the 50-70%/yr already given, or the anchor customer's agreement deferred: thesis broken, exit [14][19][21].
Oct 28-29 hyperscaler prints guide 2027 capex up and Q2 shows DC margin back near FY26's 19.4%: add per the decider's ladder [2][20][23][24].
